content.value_statement: Other Transaction budgets can mix cost shares, milestone payments, fees, and unlike price bases. This skill builds traceable workbooks with neutral comparisons and validated formulas.
actual_capabilities: Builds seven-sheet, formula-driven XLSX workbooks organized by OT milestone.
Benchmarks labor with BLS OEWS data and positions rates against CALC+ results.
Calculates project cost, performer contribution, Government share, fees, ceilings, and funding needs.
Models low, working, and high scenarios from documented assumptions.
Validates workbook structure and independently recomputes expected values with bundled Python scripts.
limitations: Requires user-supplied authority, cost-share terms, fee treatment, milestones, and other agreement facts.
Does not make legal, eligibility, price-reasonableness, or negotiation determinations.
Needs configured BLS OEWS, GSA CALC+, and applicable GSA Per Diem MCP operations.
Cannot independently execute spreadsheet formulas without Excel, LibreOffice, or another supported calculation engine.

use_cases.title: Prepare a pre-solicitation budget
use_cases.description: Build a milestone-based should-cost and funding profile before proposed prices are available.

use_cases.title: Compare a proposed amount
use_cases.description: Normalize the proposal basis and present neutral variances, benchmarks, and scenario positions.

use_cases.title: Plan performer cost sharing
use_cases.description: Model cash and in-kind contributions by milestone while preserving approved ratios and fee treatment.

prompt_templates.title: Start an OT cost estimate
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an OT cost estimate from these approved milestones: [milestones]. Ask me for missing authority, contribution, staffing, location, and fee inputs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner estimate from an approved milestone plan

prompt_templates.title: Create a pre-solicitation workbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a pre-solicitation workbook for a [research/prototype/production] OT. Use [authority path] and this approved performer contribution: [terms].

prompt_templates.title: Compare a proposal neutrally
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this proposed amount without making a price-reasonableness determination. Confirm its basis, then show variance, benchmarks, scenarios, and missing evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Model mixed milestone economics
prompt_templates.prompt: Model fixed and cost-type milestones using these approved ceilings, contribution terms, fees, labor assumptions, materials, travel, and funding dates: [inputs].
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced multi-basis funding and sensitivity analysis

output_examples.input: Prototype OT with three milestones, a one-third performer share, and no proposal.
output_examples.output: A seven-sheet workbook showing milestone costs, contributions, scenarios, labor benchmarks, methodology, raw source records, and a cumulative Government funding profile.

output_examples.input: Cost-type proposal with an approved ceiling and a user-supplied administrative fee.
output: Independent should-cost and ceiling views use the same contribution basis.
The fee is displayed separately using the supplied rate, base, timing, and treatment.
Proposal variance is presented without a fair-and-reasonable conclusion.

output_examples.input: Concept-stage research OT with incomplete milestones and multiple performer locations.
output_examples.output: A candidate milestone table for approval, followed by location-specific labor benchmarking only after the user confirms the structure.

best_practices: Provide the approved authority, contribution arrangement, milestone structure, proposal basis, and fee treatment before calculation.
Keep each performer and location separate when selecting labor benchmarks.
Run structural, independent recomputation, and real spreadsheet engine validation before delivery.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to choose statutory authority or determine participant eligibility.
Do not compare a Government funding request directly with total project cost.
Do not invent burden rates, fees, learning curves, cost shares, or specialty premiums.

faq.question: Can this skill produce a FAR-based IGCE?
faq.answer: No. It is limited to Other Transaction cost analysis and does not produce FAR 15.404 analyses.

faq.question: Can it decide whether a proposed price is reasonable?
faq.answer: No. It presents neutral evidence, variances, and scenarios while leaving the determination to the Agreements Officer.

faq.question: Which data services are required?
faq.answer: A build requires BLS OEWS and GSA CALC+ operations. GSA Per Diem operations are required when covered travel applies.

faq.question: Can it start without approved milestones?
faq.answer: Yes. It can propose a candidate structure, but it waits for user approval before pricing or workbook assembly.

faq.question: How are cost-type milestones handled?
faq.answer: The workbook shows independent should-cost and approved ceiling views using the same contribution basis.

faq.question: Does the workbook calculate formulas automatically?
faq.answer: The workbook contains formulas. Independent execution requires Excel, LibreOffice, or another supported calculation engine.
